reason: Clear the broken fragments first so the skin gap can be repaired. The picture shows the white blood cells surrounding them.
expectation: I expect the cells to remove debris from the wound, leaving a clearer gap; the skin probably won't be healed yet.

alternatives.reason: A new capillary branch could help supply the repair, but clearing the wound seems like a useful first step.

effect: The debris is cleared, but the wound still needs a surface, support and blood supply.
reaction: The white cells containing the fragments made the cleanup clear.
reason: Build the blood supply for the repair; the picture shows wound messengers reaching the nearby vessel and a new branch growing.
expectation: I expect a new vessel branch to grow toward the wound, though I don't know exactly how the messengers cause it.

alternatives.reason: Preparing replacement skin cells also addresses the new goal, but I want to build their supply route first.

effect: The new capillary branch is ready to add to the cleared wound.
reaction: The branch growing toward another vessel makes the supply route easier to picture.
reason: Add the sprout to the wound to continue rebuilding its blood supply.
expectation: I expect the new branch to become part of the wound's supply, though I don't know whether that completes the blood-vessel route.

alternatives.reason: Building supporting fibres also helps repair, but I want to finish the vessel project first.

effect: The new branch joins another vessel, creating a blood route that supplies nearby cells.
reaction: Seeing blood flow through the joined route makes the supply project feel complete.
reason: Build supporting fibres for the deeper wound; the picture shows the skin cells using protein building blocks to make them.
expectation: I expect the cells to produce supporting protein fibres that can later be added to the wound.

alternatives.reason: Preparing surface cells would also help close the gap, but I want to build the deeper support first.

effect: The supporting fibres are ready, but the deeper gap remains open.
reaction: The picture makes it clear the fibres still need to join the existing tissue.
reason: Add the new fibres to support the deeper wound.
expectation: I expect the fibres to connect across the deeper gap, though the skin surface may still need to close.

alternatives.reason: Preparing surface cells also helps close the wound, but I want to finish the support first.

effect: The deeper wound now has support and a blood supply; the surface still needs to close and the clot must be cleared.
reaction: The fibres fill only part of the wound, so the repair still feels unfinished.
reason: Prepare replacement surface cells using the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the supplied cells to divide and move toward the gap, using oxygen and nutrients; they may still need to be added to the wound.

effect: New skin cells are ready beside the wound, but the surface gap remains open.
reaction: The outlined gap makes it clear where the cells need to go.
reason: Use the only offered combination to add the new cells and close the surface.
expectation: I expect the cells to spread across the gap; the temporary clot may still need clearing afterward.

effect: The skin surface is closed, but the deeper tissue is still strengthening and the temporary clot remains.
reaction: It is useful to see that a closed surface does not mean healing is finished.
reason: Use the only offered combination to clear the temporary clot; the enzyme picture shows it cutting the protein threads.
expectation: I expect the clot threads to break down now that the vessel is sealed, though the tissue may still need time to strengthen.

effect: Most clot threads are gone, while supporting fibres and a small scar remain; the scar will keep changing.
reaction: It was useful to see the temporary clot replaced by lasting tissue rather than disappearing without a trace.

mostWorthwhile.text: Closing the skin surface was most worthwhile because it showed that the gap can close while the deeper tissue is still gaining strength.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the supporting fibres and then fitting them felt a little repetitive, though the pictures distinguished making them from placing them in the wound.

surprise.text: The capillary sprout joined another vessel to form a flowing route, making it clearer how the new branch supplies cells.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. The pictures explained the purposes, though I followed the named messenger pairing without knowing exactly how it caused a vessel to grow.

continue.text: I would probably continue: seeing the surface close before deeper healing was finished made me curious about what happens next, even if some fitting steps felt repetitive.
